title: Guimbal Cabri G2
notice: The procedures are the sim's own wording for this helicopter: the checklist items and clues of the Cabri G2 (its language file) and the instructor texts of the sim's eleven helicopter lessons, which fly this aircraft; every step names the key it comes from. The language file gives the wording and the numbers (NR 530 RPM, 45 and 50 kt, 300 ft, 500 ft) but not the order of the items: the order of the walkaround and of the start follows the logic of the clues (the clutch before the checks that need the rotor turning) and is ours, as is the order of the shutdown. The master and governor steps are marked as technique where the sim does not list them. The guide has not been run on the helicopter and none of its controls is marked verified: the ticks read standard simulation variables (the ones the aircraft's own templates use) that the aircraft may not drive. There is no procedure for an engine failure or an autorotation: the files that can be read offline do not contain one.

wa_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
wa_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
wa_ground.help: The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

wa_air.title: Flying
wa_air.text: The walkaround is done on the ground, before the flight.

wa_covers.title: Covers
wa_covers.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Remove the three blade socks from the main rotor blades.
steps.why: The sim's solo lesson: "Go through your pre-flight checklist thoroughly, don't forget to remove covers."

steps.text: Remove the pitot and static port covers (plugs) and check their condition.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_PITOT_TUBE_AND_STATIC_PRESSURE_PORT; Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_REMOVE_PLUGS_CHECK_CONDITION

wa_engine.title: Engine and main gearbox
wa_engine.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Open the left engine cowling and check behind it.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_BEHIND_LEFT_ENGINE_COWLING

steps.text: Open the right engine cowling and check behind it.
Check the air intake and the main gearbox compartment.
Pull the dipstick out. The oil level must be between 4 and 6 Qt. Tighten the dipstick back in place.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CLUE.DIPSTICK_OUT_OIL_LEVEL_4_AND_6_QT

steps.text: Check the oil level in the sight gauge: it must be at the mid-sight gauge minimum.
Close and lock the front latch, then both side latches of the cowlings.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_CLOSE_AND_LOCK_FRONT_LATCH; Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_CLOSE_AND_LOCK_BOTH_LATCHES

wa_fuel.title: Fuel
wa_fuel.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Check the fuel pump and its hose.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_FUEL_PUMP_AND_HOSE

steps.text: Drain the gascolator.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_GASCOLATOR_DRAIN

steps.text: Check the fuel quantity.
steps.why: The sim's instructor: before taking off, check that all gauges are green and that there is enough fuel.

wa_outside.title: Skids, windows, lights, luggage
wa_outside.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Check the landing gear pants and the skids.
Check the lower windows.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_LOWER_WINDOWS

steps.text: Check the landing light and the navigation light.
Check the inside of the luggage compartment.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_INSIDE_LUGGAGE_COMPARTMENT

steps.text: Close and lock the luggage door.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): GAME.CHECKLIST_LUGGAGE_DOOR

wa_done.title: Walkaround done
wa_done.text: Get in and buckle up. Go on with the engine start.

es_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
es_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
es_ground.help: The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

es_air.title: Flying
es_air.text: Do not start the engine in flight. Use the sim's own procedures if the engine stopped.

es_pre.title: Before the start
es_pre.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Lower the collective all the way down.
steps.why: The sim's instructor: before starting the engine, lower the collective all the way down.

steps.text: Pull the rotor brake lever fully backward, check that the indicator is on, then lock the lever fully forward.
Check that the GOV OFF light is on.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.CHECK_GOV_OFF_LIGHT_ON

steps.text: If the engine is cold, OAT, CHT, OIL T and CARB T must show the same temperature.
Switch the master on.
steps.why: Technique, not a checklist item: the sim's checklist file has no master item. The tooltip names the switch "Master"; the plasma ignition, the starter and the EPM need power.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): AIRCRAFT.TOOLTIPS.TITLE.ENGINE_MASTER

es_start.title: Start
es_start.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Switch the plasma ignition on and check the beeper.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.SWITCH_PLASMA_IGNITION_ON

steps.text: Switch the magneto on.
steps.why: The sim's item is "Ignition switches"; its clue switches both the plasma and the magneto switches off at shutdown, so both are on for the start.

steps.text: For injections, raise the collective to 1/3, then roll the twist grip back and forth 2 to 3 times.
steps.why: The sim's clue gives no condition for this item.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.INJECTIONS_COLLECTIVE

steps.text: Press the starter button. The STARTER light must light on, then back off.
The oil pressure annunciator must light off within 30 seconds of starting.
Set the throttle to get around 2000 RPM.
The ALT light must be off.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.ALT_LIGHT_OFF

steps.text: No alarms must be displayed, except OIL P, FUEL P, OIL T and CARB T (if the outside temperature corresponds).
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.NO_ALARMS_DISPLAYED_EXCEPT

es_clutch.title: Rotor
es_clutch.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: At idle power, the engine RPM and NR must be desynchronized: the needles apart.
Open the cover of the clutch switch.
steps.why: The clutch switch sits under a cover (the L: variable XMLVAR_ROTORCRAFT_Clutch_Cover_Opened); the switch only works while the cover is open.

steps.text: Engage the clutch and lock the switch. The CLUTCH light must light on.
Wait for the CLUTCH light to light off.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.CLUTCH_LIGHT_LIGHT_OFF; Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.FEEDBACK.WAITING_CLUTCH_LIGHT_OFF

steps.text: Check that the rotor and engine indicators are synchronized.
While the engine warms up, set the throttle to keep NR between 420 and 450 RPM, below 450.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.SET_THROTTLE_LEVER_NR_BETWEEN_420_450_RPM; Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.MAINTAIN_NR_BELOW_450_RPM

steps.text: Switch the governor on.
steps.why: Technique, not a checklist item: the sim checks the GOV OFF light before the start and the governor engaging at NR 400 RPM, and does not list the switch itself or when to set it.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.GAME.CHECKLIST_GOV_OFF_LIGHT

steps.text: Increase power. Check that the governor engages from NR 400 RPM.
Set the throttle to get NR around 530 RPM.

es_runup.title: Checks before takeoff
es_runup.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Set the carburetor heat switch to HOT. Check that the additional carb brick pops and NR drops.
Set the carburetor heat switch to COLD. Check that the additional carb brick disappears and NR increases.
Switch the plasma ignition off: the engine RPM should drop by about 300. Then switch it back on.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.PLASMA_OFF_RPM_DROP

steps.text: The warning horn must work when NR is near the lower red limit.
The lower BARC light must blink when NR is in the yellow arc.
Check the oil temperature: 30 °C (86 °F) minimum is recommended, 60 °C (140 °F) minimum for maximum power.
Check that all gauges are green and that the fuel is enough.
Set NR around 530 RPM again.

es_done.title: Ready
es_done.text: The engine runs, the rotor turns at NR 530 RPM and the checks are done. Take off to a hover.

hv_start.title: What do you want?
hv_start.text: What do you want to do?

choices.label: Hold the hover and hover taxi

hv_up.title: Take off to a hover
hv_up.source: Sim lesson "collective" (fs24-asobo-trainings-helicopter-collective, en-us.locpak): Collective.Briefing.Long and Collective.Dlg.State1/State2

steps.text: Look left and right: no people or vehicles may approach.
Raise the collective slowly until the helicopter is light on the skids, at about 65 percent of the available power.
At first the power indication does not move. Keep raising the collective slowly: too fast makes a sloppy takeoff.
Once the helicopter leaves the ground, let it rise to a hover at 2 ft skid height. Look into the distance and be very gentle.
Keep the heading with the pedals. The rotor turns clockwise and the nose yaws left, so press the right pedal as you raise the collective.
Keep the position with the cyclic. The Cabri drifts left in a hover, so expect a little right pressure.
Note where the power needle stands in the hover (the MLI): that is the power to hover, and it changes with weight, wind, elevation and temperature.

hv_hold.title: Hold the hover
hv_hold.source: Sim lesson "hover" (fs24-asobo-trainings-helicopter-hover, en-us.locpak): Hover.Dlg.State2 and Hover.Briefing.Long

steps.text: Cyclic: eliminate drift in the horizontal plane.
Collective: maintain the altitude.
Pedals: control the nose direction.
Never stop making small corrections: a helicopter is dynamically unstable.
Move the controls as gently as possible.
Adjusting one control needs an adjustment of the other two; this is what makes the hover hard.
Stay below 8 ft in a stationary hover near the ground and in a hover taxi: if the engine quits higher without airspeed, you cannot land safely.
To turn on the spot, press the right pedal to turn right; to turn left, ease the right pedal or press the left one. Press the opposite pedal to stop the turn.

hv_taxi.title: Hover taxi
hv_taxi.source: Sim lesson "hover" (fs24-asobo-trainings-helicopter-hover, en-us.locpak): Hover.Briefing.Long and Hover.Dlg.State3

steps.text: Hover taxi is for moving below 25 ft AGL. Move at the speed of a brisk walk and keep every input very gentle.
Stay at a hovering altitude of 2 to 8 ft.
When you move faster the rotor gets more effective and lifts you: lower the collective to keep your height. When you slow down, raise it again.
At 16 to 24 kt the rotor gains translational lift: the nose rises. Apply slight forward cyclic and reduce the right pedal to keep the heading.
Hover taxi to the helipad and turn into the wind: find the windsock. A headwind is always preferred.
Make sure no other aircraft are on the taxiways you cross.
Ease the cyclic forward smoothly and slowly. Raise the collective as needed so that the helicopter does not sink.
Accelerate at a constant height below 10 ft toward 45 kt.
Through translational lift the nose tends to rise: apply enough forward cyclic. The faster you are, the less right pedal you need.
Rotate at 45 kt.
Climb at 50 kt and keep 50 kt for the whole climb. Put the helicopter in trim.
Below 100 ft keep the rate of climb at or below 500 fpm, so that an engine failure is easier to handle.
Raise the collective for a more effective climb, but never over 100 percent of the available power.
Turn right at 300 ft AGL, still climbing: the helicopter pattern has right turns.
At 500 ft AGL level off at 70 kt and turn right onto the downwind leg.
The attitude of the rotor disk sets the airspeed; the collective sets the altitude.
Speed up: push the cyclic forward and raise the collective to keep the altitude. Slow down: pull the cyclic back and lower the collective.
Fly at 80 kt. Keep the horizon in the same place on the windshield to keep the speed.
Find the cyclic position for the attitude, then trim the force away. Use the cyclic to fly and the trim to relieve the forces, not the trim to fly.
Turn: apply sideward pressure on the cyclic in the direction of the turn. The pedals are not needed to turn.
Keep the ball and the yaw string centered with the pedals (no slip, no skid).
After the bank angle is set, return the cyclic to neutral. Add forward cyclic for the speed and raise the collective for the altitude and the rotor speed.
To roll out, apply cyclic pressure the opposite way.
Look around before every turn.

ap_steps.title: Pattern and approach to a hover

steps.text: On the downwind leg keep 500 ft AGL and 70 kt.
steps.why: At Grenoble Le Versoud 500 ft AGL is about 1200 ft MSL; the sim's lesson says the traffic pattern altitude differs by airport.

steps.text: Abeam the helipad start to slow down to 60 kt. Lower the collective a little so that you do not climb.
Look around, then turn right onto base. Keep the turn coordinated.
Begin the descent. Arrive on final at 300 ft AGL and 50 kt.
On final, lower the collective enough to decelerate and descend along the approach angle. A normal approach is 7 to 12 degrees.
Control the speed with the cyclic and the angle with the collective. With less collective the nose pitches down: use aft cyclic to keep 50 kt.
Keep the angle constant to the helipad. If the landing zone moves up in the windshield the approach is shallow; if it moves down it is too steep.
Keep at least 30 kt until the rate of descent is below 300 fpm, to avoid the vortex ring state.
Keep decelerating with aft cyclic to the speed of a brisk walk. Lower the collective gently to keep the angle.
At about 25 kt the translational lift is lost: raise the collective to prevent settling and push the cyclic forward for the right rate of closure.
Arrive over the helipad with the rate of descent and the ground speed reaching zero at the same time. Refer to the ground speed.
Near 2 ft raise the collective enough to hover and apply aft cyclic to stop the forward movement.

ld_steps.title: Land from a hover
ld_steps.source: Sim lesson "collective" (fs24-asobo-trainings-helicopter-collective, en-us.locpak): Collective.Briefing.Long and Collective.Dlg.State4

steps.text: Stabilize the hover at 2 ft.
Make sure there is no movement and no yawing before you touch the ground.
Lower the collective gently while you keep the heading and the position over the landing spot. Look into the distance.
The helicopter hits an air cushion and wants to bob back up. Let it, and the next time it lowers, reduce the collective even more.
Avoid any lateral or yaw movement on landing, and hover high enough for skid clearance: this avoids a dynamic rollover.
When the skids are on the ground, lower the collective all the way down.

sd_ground.title: Where is the aircraft?
sd_ground.text: Is the aircraft on the ground?
sd_ground.help: The answer is filled in from the simulator when it can tell.

sd_steps.title: Shutdown
sd_steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.* and GAME.CHECKLIST_*

steps.text: Leave the collective in the most downward position.
Wait for the cylinder head temperature to drop below 180 °C.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.WAIT_CHT_BELOW_180_C

steps.text: Switch the clutch off. The CLUTCH light must light off within 10 seconds of the disengagement.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.SWITCH_CLUTCH_OFF

steps.text: Switch the landing and navigation lights off.
Switch the plasma and magneto switches off.
The rotor can be braked when NR is below 150 RPM (the white mark). The rotor brake speeds up the stopping of the main rotor.
steps.source: Cabri G2 language file (fs24-asobo-aircraft-cabri-g2, en-us.locpak): CHECKLIST.CLUE.ROTOR_CAN_BE_BRAKED; Sim lesson "solo" (fs24-asobo-trainings-helicopter-solo, en-us.locpak): Solo.Dlg.State2.AfterFlight010.RotorBrake

sd_done.title: Shut down
sd_done.text: The engine is off and the rotor is stopped.

steps.text: Make a clearing turn to visually clear the area, then check the gauges: no warning lights, RPM in the green, fuel as required.
From a normal hover height, push the cyclic forward. Reach 45 kt with the cyclic, stay under 10 ft with the collective and keep the heading with the pedals.
As the speed nears 45 kt, apply gentle aft cyclic to climb, then lower the collective and level off at 30 ft. Keep 45 kt and 30 ft.
Pick a visual reference as the place to stop.
Apply aft cyclic and lower the collective as needed to keep the entry altitude through the deceleration. Add left pedal for the heading. The timing must be exact.
If the helicopter balloons, lower the collective more or use less aft cyclic.
As the speed falls the helicopter begins to settle: raise the collective slowly to control the descent.
Add gentle forward cyclic to level the helicopter and keep the heading with the pedals.
Raise the collective and add left pedal to come to a hover at 2 ft.
Fly the high reconnaissance at 1000 to 1200 ft over the area, then low and slow alongside it.
Find the wind direction and speed, a suitable touchdown point and the suitability of the landing area.
Look for wires and their supporting structures, the approach and departure axes, and any obstacles on both.
Find forced landing areas for an emergency.
Be at 1000 ft and 50 kt when you enter the final descent.
A steep approach is 13 to 15 degrees (a normal one 7 to 12). Lower the collective more than for a normal approach.
Avoid the vortex ring state: do not go slower than 30 kt with more than 300 fpm of descent and 20 to 100 percent of the power.
The translational lift is lost higher: raise the collective earlier and more forcefully to avoid settling.
Be ready to terminate the approach if the area suddenly looks unsafe.
Reposition to the most downwind part of the area, for a longer takeoff climb, and turn into the wind.
Hover and check that you have at least 10 percent of excess power: the difference between the power available and the power to hover.

The takeoff is possible when the distance between the rotor disc and the top of the obstacle is at least a third of the distance between the rotor disc and the base of the obstacle, seen from the pilot's seat.
Slowly raise the collective to the maximum power available and lower the nose to gain speed. Aim for 100 percent on the MLI, not more.
The large collective movement needs much more pedal pressure to keep the heading.
Keep the rotor RPM at its maximum. Use the cyclic to control the climb angle and keep the distance between the rotor disc and the obstacle.
When the obstacle is out of view, continue with a normal climb: 90 percent on the MLI or the maximum power available, 50 kt.

hz_steps.title: Keep in mind
hz_steps.source: Sim lesson "intro" (fs24-asobo-trainings-helicopter-intro, en-us.locpak): Intro.Dlg.State2 and the other lessons named in each step

steps.text: Never exceed 130 kt. The airspeed caution range ends at 45 kt, so be careful when flying slow.
Never go over 100 percent of the power on the MLI: too much collective stalls the rotor and the helicopter settles into its own downwash.

Keep the rotor RPM constant: raising the collective lowers it, lowering the collective raises it. In normal operation the correlator and the governor keep it constant, with no manual throttle adjustment.
Vortex ring state: a descent of at least 300 fpm, with 20 to 100 percent power and a speed below translational lift (16 to 24 kt). Keep 30 kt until the descent is below 300 fpm.
Watch the vertical speed, especially on descent.
Dynamic rollover: once it starts it cannot be stopped by opposite cyclic alone. Avoid lateral or yaw movements on takeoff and landing, and hover high enough for skid clearance.
Stay below 8 ft in a stationary hover or hover taxi. Above it, an engine failure without airspeed means no safe landing.
Avoid the shaded areas of the height / velocity diagram on takeoff: accelerate at a constant height below 10 ft.
Keep the fuselage streamlined: ball and yaw string centered.
